This is a '''timeline of the theory of [[abelian varieties]]''' in [[algebraic geometry]], including elliptic curves.

==Early history==
* 3rd century AD [[Diophantus]] of Alexandria studies rational points on elliptic curves

* c. 1000 [[Al-Karaji]] writes on [[congruent number]]s<ref>[http://www.cms.math.ca/Events/summer05/abs/pdf/hm.pdf PDF]</ref>

==Seventeenth century==
* Fermat studies [[Proof by infinite descent|descent for elliptic curves]]
* 1643 Fermat poses an elliptic curve [[Diophantine equation]]<ref>[http://www.mathpages.com/home/kmath022/kmath022.htm Miscellaneous Diophantine Equations] at MathPages</ref>{{unreliable source?|date=November 2011}}
* 1670 Fermat's son published his ''Diophantus'' with notes

==Eighteenth century==
* 1718  [[Giulio Carlo Fagnano dei Toschi]], studies the rectification of the [[Lemniscate of Bernoulli|lemniscate]], addition results for [[elliptic integral]]s.<ref>[http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Fagnano_Giulio.html Fagnano_Giulio biography<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>
* 1736 [[Leonhard Euler]] writes on the [[Pendulum (mathematics)#Arbitrary-amplitude period|pendulum equation]] without the small-angle approximation.<ref>[[E. T. Whittaker]], ''[[A Treatise on the Analytical Dynamics of Particles and Rigid Bodies]]'' (fourth edition 1937), p. 72.</ref>
* 1738 Euler writes on curves of genus 1 considered by Fermat and [[Frenicle]]
* 1750 Euler writes on elliptic integrals
* 23 December 1751 – 27 January 1752: Birth of the theory of [[elliptic function]]s, according to later remarks of Jacobi, as Euler writes on Fagnano's work.<ref>[[André Weil]], ''Number Theory: An approach through history'' (1984), p. 1.</ref>
* 1775 [[John Landen]] publishes [[Landen's transformation]],<ref>[http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Landen.html Landen biography<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> an [[isogeny]] formula.
* 1786 [[Adrien-Marie Legendre]] begins to write on [[elliptic integral]]s
* 1797 [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]] discovers [[double periodicity]] of the [[lemniscate function]]<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20091027124329/http://www.geocities.com/RainForest/Vines/2977/gauss/appendix/chrono.html Chronology of the Life of Carl F. Gauss<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>
* 1799 Gauss finds the connection of the length of a lemniscate and a case of the [[arithmetic-geometric mean]], giving a numerical method for a [[complete elliptic integral]].<ref>Semen Grigorʹevich
Gindikin, ''Tales of Physicists and Mathematicians'' (1988 translation), p. 143.</ref>

==Nineteenth century==
* 1826 [[Niels Henrik Abel]], [[Abel-Jacobi map]]
* 1827 [[Inversion of elliptic integral]]s independently by Abel and [[Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi]]
* 1829 Jacobi, ''Fundamenta nova theoriae functionum ellipticarum'', introduces four [[theta function]]s of one variable
* 1835 Jacobi points out the use of the group law for [[diophantine geometry]], in ''De usu Theoriae Integralium Ellipticorum et Integralium Abelianorum in Analysi Diophantea''<ref>[[Dale Husemoller]], ''Elliptic Curves''.</ref>
* 1836-7 [[Friedrich Julius Richelot]], the [[Richelot isogeny]].<ref>Richelot, ''Essai sur une méthode générale pour déterminer les valeurs des intégrales ultra-elliptiques, fondée sur des transformations remarquables de ces transcendantes'', [[Comptes rendus de l'Académie des Sciences|C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris.]] 2 (1836), 622-627; ''De transformatione integralium Abelianorum primi ordinis commentatio'', [[Crelle's Journal|J. Reine Angew. Math.]] 16 (1837), 221-341.</ref>
* 1847 [[Adolph Göpel]] gives the equation of the [[Kummer surface]]<ref>[http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Gopel.html Gopel biography<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>
* 1851 [[Johann Georg Rosenhain]] writes a prize essay on the inversion problem in genus 2.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gap-system.org/~history/Biographies/Rosenhain.html |title=Rosenhain biography |website=www.gap-system.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080907030500/http://www.gap-system.org/~history/Biographies/Rosenhain.html |archive-date=2008-09-07}}</ref>
*c. 1850 [[Thomas Weddle]] - [[Weddle surface]]
* 1856 [[Weierstrass elliptic function]]s
* 1857 [[Bernhard Riemann]]<ref>''Theorie der Abel'schen Funktionen, [[Crelle's Journal|J. Reine Angew. Math.]] 54 (1857), 115-180''</ref> lays the foundations for further work on abelian varieties in dimension > 1, introducing the [[Riemann bilinear relations]] and [[Riemann theta function]].
* 1865 [[Carl Johannes Thomae]], ''Theorie der ultraelliptischen Funktionen und Integrale erster und zweiter Ordnung''<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gap-system.org/~history/Biographies/Thomae.html |title=Thomae biography |website=www.gap-system.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060928083844/http://www.gap-system.org/~history/Biographies/Thomae.html |archive-date=2006-09-28}}</ref>
* 1866 [[Alfred Clebsch]] and [[Paul Gordan]], ''Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen''
* 1869 [[Karl Weierstrass]] proves an [[abelian function]] satisfies an [[algebraic addition theorem]]
* 1879, [[Charles Auguste Briot]], ''Théorie des fonctions abéliennes''
* 1880 In a letter to [[Richard Dedekind]], [[Leopold Kronecker]] describes his ''[[Kronecker's Jugendtraum|Jugendtraum]]'',<ref>[http://www.sunsite.ubc.ca/DigitalMathArchive/Langlands/pdf/jugend-ps.pdf ''Some Contemporary Problems with Origins in the Jugendtraum''], [[Robert Langlands]]</ref> to use [[complex multiplication]] theory to generate [[abelian extension]]s of [[imaginary quadratic field]]s
* 1884 [[Sofia Kovalevskaya]] writes on the [[reduction of abelian functions to elliptic functions]]<ref>''Über die Reduction einer bestimmten Klasse Abel'scher Integrale Ranges auf elliptische Integrale,'' [[Acta Mathematica]] 4, 392–414 (1884).</ref>
* 1888 [[Friedrich Schottky]] finds a non-trivial condition on the [[theta constant]]s for curves of genus <math>g = 4</math>, launching the [[Schottky problem]].
* 1891 [[Appell–Humbert theorem]] of [[Paul Émile Appell]] and [[Georges Humbert]], classifies the [[holomorphic line bundle]]s on an [[abelian surface]] by [[cocycle]] data.
* 1894 ''Die Entwicklung der Theorie der algebräischen Functionen in älterer und neuerer Zeit'', report by [[Alexander von Brill]] and [[Max Noether]]
* 1895 [[Wilhelm Wirtinger]], ''Untersuchungen über Thetafunktionen'', studies [[Prym variety|Prym varieties]]
* 1897 [[H. F. Baker]], ''Abelian Functions: Abel's Theorem and the Allied Theory of Theta Functions''

==Twentieth century==
* c.1910 The theory of [[Poincaré normal function]]s implies that the [[Picard variety]] and [[Albanese variety]] are [[isogeny|isogenous]].<ref>[http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS/Repository/1.0/Disseminate?view=body&id=pdf_1&handle=euclid.bams/1183548682 PDF], p. 168.</ref>
*1913 [[Torelli's theorem]]<ref>[[Ruggiero Torelli]], ''Sulle varietà di Jacobi'', Rend. della R. Acc. Nazionale dei Lincei (5), 22, 1913, 98–103.</ref>
* 1916 [[Gaetano Scorza]]<ref>[[Gaetano Scorza]], Intorno alla teoria generale delle matrici di Riemann e ad alcune sue applicazioni, Rend. del Circolo Mat. di Palermo 41 (1916)</ref> applies the term "abelian variety" to [[complex tori]].
* 1921 [[Solomon Lefschetz]] shows that any complex torus with Riemann matrix satisfying the necessary conditions can be embedded in some [[complex projective space]] using theta-functions
* 1922 [[Louis Mordell]] proves [[Mordell's theorem]]: the rational points on an elliptic curve over the rational numbers form a [[finitely-generated abelian group]]
*1929 [[Arthur B. Coble]], ''Algebraic Geometry and Theta Functions''
*1939 [[Siegel modular form]]s<ref>[[Carl Ludwig Siegel]], ''Einführung in die Theorie der Modulfunktionen ''n''-ten Grades'', [[Mathematische Annalen]] 116 (1939), 617–657</ref>
* c. 1940 [[André Weil]] defines "abelian variety"
* 1952 Weil defines an [[intermediate Jacobian]]
* [[Theorem of the cube]]
* [[Selmer group]]
* [[Michael Atiyah]] classifies [[holomorphic vector bundle]]s on an elliptic curve
* 1961 [[Goro Shimura]] and [[Yutaka Taniyama]], ''Complex Multiplication of Abelian Varieties and its Applications to Number Theory''
* [[Néron model]]
* [[Birch–Swinnerton–Dyer conjecture]]
* [[Moduli space for abelian varieties]]
* [[Duality of abelian varieties]]
* c.1967 [[David Mumford]] develops a new theory of the [[equations defining abelian varieties]]
* 1968 [[Serre–Tate theorem on good reduction]] extends the results of [[Max Deuring]] on elliptic curves to the abelian variety case.<ref>[[Jean-Pierre Serre]] and [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]], ''Good Reduction of Abelian Varieties'', [[Annals of Mathematics]], Second Series, Vol. 88, No. 3 (Nov., 1968), pp. 492–517.</ref>
*c. 1980 [[Mukai–Fourier transform]]: the [[Dual abelian variety#Poincaré line bundle|Poincaré line bundle]] as Mukai–Fourier kernel induces an equivalence of the [[derived categories]] of [[coherent sheaves]] for an abelian variety and its dual.<ref>[[Daniel Huybrechts]], ''Fourier–Mukai transforms in algebraic geometry'' (2006), Ch. 9.</ref>
*1983 [[Takahiro Shiota]] proves [[Novikov's conjecture on the Schottky problem]]
*1985 [[Jean-Marc Fontaine]] shows that any positive-dimensional abelian variety over the rationals has bad reduction somewhere.<ref>[[Jean-Marc Fontaine]], ''Il n'y a pas de variété abélienne sur Z'', [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] (1985) no. 3, 515–538.</ref>

==Twenty-first century==
* 2001 Proof of the [[modularity theorem]] for elliptic curves is completed.
